previous_catalog_record.summary: 0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~10-14) with 2-4 PAIRS OF TWO OPPOSITE 3×3-BOX CORNERS — for each pair: pick a 3×3 BOX with top-left at random (r0, c0); pick one of TWO DIAGONAL ORIENTATIONS — either MAIN diagonal (corners (r0, c0) and (r0+2, c0+2)) or ANTI diagonal (corners (r0, c0+2) and (r0+2, c0)); PAINT those two corners with the pair's distinct non-0 color (drawn from a shuffled {1..9}). The 3×3 boxes are tracked in a used cell set so pairs' boxes do not overlap (each pair's full 9 cells are reserved). The middle cells of the box and the off-diagonal corners stay bg-0. Rule (EXPAND EACH PAIR OF OPPOSITE 3×3 BOX CORNERS INTO A FULL X — DRAW BOTH DIAGONALS): for EACH color C that appears EXACTLY TWICE at OPPOSITE CORNERS OF A 3×3 BOX: identify the 3×3 BOX. PAINT both diagonals of that box (the main diagonal and the anti-diagonal — 5 cells total, since they share the center) with COLOR C. The middle cell at the box center becomes C. Net: each 2-cell diagonal-corner pair blooms into a 5-cell colored X spanning the 3×3 box.

sequential_dependency.intermediate: The input-dependent orientation map from each color to main or anti diagonal.
sequential_dependency.step_a: For each active color, locate its two opposite 3x3-box corners and classify the pair as main-diagonal or anti-diagonal.
sequential_dependency.step_b: Complete main-diagonal pairs as five-cell X motifs and anti-diagonal pairs as five-cell plus motifs.
sequential_dependency.why_b_depends_on_a: The motif for each color cannot be chosen before Step A identifies that color pair's orientation; different colors in the same input can require different completions.
